chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is recommended for the first-timer that he walks to the Sacred Monument and enters the House.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: A pilgrim performing Hajj for the first time
key_terms.الْمَشْعَر الْحَرَام: The Sacred Monument (specifically Mash'ar al-Haram in Muzdalifah)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for a first-time pilgrim during Hajj?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the specific ritual etiquette for the first-time pilgrim (al-sarrurah) during the Muzdalifa phase of Hajj. It emphasizes the recommendation to physically tread upon the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram) and enter the Kaaba, reflecting the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between obligatory pillars and recommended acts that enhance the spiritual completeness of the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is recommended for the first-timer that he walks to the Sacred Monuments, and if he enters the House (Kabah)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is preferable for al-Sarura (one who performs al-Hajj for the first time) to walk on al-Mash‘ar al-Haram (name of a place) and enter the House. ’’’(Fatwa best explains Hadith 2-3 of this Chapter.)
